doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Early rock and roll, R&B and Stan Freberg
summary: His taste in rhythm and blues over Elvis and a laugh about Stan Freberg's Heartbreak Hotel parody.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I see. What about the early rock & roll?

Well rock & roll was happening, started happening when I already loved west coast jazz. And you know Elvis’s first records came out. But I used to listen to a lot of rhythm & blues you know, Fats Domino and Chuck Berry, Bo Diddley, and the blues, the Howlin’ Wolf and Muddy Waters and all those guys. And they put out singles but they were considered race records. It hadn’t crossed over at that point, until later. And I loved that stuff, and I thought Elvis was — I said Elvis is very good. I really liked him, but he was kind of a shadow of those guys. You know he wasn’t — and he even said that you know. It was pretty obvious that he was indebted to all those real, you know southern blues singers and rhythm & blues singers. And then I started buying those records. But I didn’t — I never really bought Elvis’s records. He was on the radio a lot and I liked some of his stuff. Some of it was very funny too because it was parodied by guys like Stan Freberg — do you know who that was?
Stan Freberg does a take-off on “Heartbreak Hotel.” He did take-offs on a lot of people. He did Lawrence Welk and — but the “Heartbreak Hotel” was, you know the echo. “Too
